objective:
Make the `/` handler in src/server.ts survive a snapshot file that cannot be read, parsed or rendered (#10). For the requested date (?date= or newest): try readFile + JSON.parse + renderPage inside try/catch. On failure, walk the older dates in the listing (newest first) and render the first one that succeeds, passing a new optional 4th argument to renderPage, `notice?: { failedDate: string }`. When notice is given, renderPage prints, in the hero where the `old` line goes (and instead of the 'You're looking at … See today' line, since / would loop back), exactly: `

The status saved for {failedDate} could not be opened, so this shows {s.date}, the most recent earlier day that could. The file that could not be opened

` (dates escaped, link built with the existing `a()` helper if it fits). The history footer still lists every date. If no date can be rendered at all, reply text/plain 503: `The saved status for {date} could not be opened, and no earlier day could be opened either.` Never send a raw 500 or the parse error message to the client; log the error with app.log.error.
contract: Measured at 972c3f2: pnpm test → 72 passed. Today `/` does `JSON.parse(await readFile(...))` with no catch (src/server.ts, inlined), so a truncated newest file gives `500 application/json {"statusCode":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","message":"Unexpected end of JSON input"}` (reviewer of #5, brief 003). Decisions: fall back to the next readable older day with a plain-words notice and a link to the damaged file (P-4); keep the client wording exactly as given in the objective — do not reword it (the user signs off on it at PR time). A file that parses but lacks fields renderPage needs counts as damaged too (catch render errors, not just parse errors). Keep `date` only ever chosen from the directory listing (existing #5 guarantee). test/page/server.test.ts already builds scratch snapshot dirs with writeFileSync via `snapshotsDir(dates)`; add damaged cases there (or a sibling helper) writing e.g. `{"schemaVersion":1,"da` as the file body. isLatest stays true-for-newest semantics for the normal path; on the fallback path the notice replaces the old-line.
negative: Do not edit files outside scope: src/types.ts, glossary.json, snapshots/, test/fixtures/, docs, .github, render.yaml, root files and the lockfile belong to the coordinator.
No new dependencies. No live network calls in tests. Never read, print or commit a token or key (P-6).
rubric: Tests first (red then green): (a) truncated newest file + readable older day → 200 text/html, contains the notice with both dates and the GitHub link to the damaged file, renders the older day's content, no 'Internal Server Error'/'Unexpected end' text; (b) ?date= pointing at a damaged older day → same fallback to the next older readable day; (c) valid JSON missing required fields (e.g. `{}`) → treated as damaged; (d) every file damaged → 503 text/plain with the exact sentence; (e) normal path unchanged (existing tests still pass); (f) behind a password the fallback still requires auth (401 without it).
renderPage called without notice produces byte-identical HTML to before (existing render tests pass unchanged; every committed snapshot still renders, O-4).
Client wording matches the objective character for character.
pnpm test and pnpm typecheck clean from the repo root.
